description: General-purpose inverters with Modbus RTU on the RS-485 port
source: Fuji Electric FRENIC RS-485 User's Manual, document 24A7-E-0082 (MEH448)
notes: The address of a function code is its group number times 256 plus its number: F01 is 0x0001, S01 is 0x0701, M01 is 0x0801, y01 is 0x0E01 (groups: F 0, E 1, C 2, P 3, H 4, A 5, o 6, S 7, M 8, r 10, J 13, y 14, W 15, X 16, Z 17, b 18, d 19).

This map lists the communications dedicated codes S and M that all four families support, the link-function codes y01 to y10, y98 and y99, and a few F codes. The W, X and Z keypad mirrors, the other F, E, C, P, H and A codes and the model-specific S and M codes (torque, PG, option, motor temperature) are in the manual.

Reading 03 returns up to 50 words (100 on MEGA) and does not cross a function code group; unused codes read as 0. Function 06 writes one register and 16 several; coils are not supported by FRENIC-Mini.

Data formats: integers use format 1, 0.1 units format 3, 0.01 units format 5 or 22, and the per-unit values (S01, S12, S13, M01, M06, M27, M32, M49, M50, M68) are +/-20000 = 100 % or the maximum frequency.

To run the inverter over Modbus the link must be valid: set H30 (and y98, y99) so that the frequency and operation commands come from communications; y99 = 1, 2 or 3 does the same from the host without changing H30.
The manual does not give the factory serial settings; the connection defaults here are the format's defaults. Parity y06 = 0 (no parity) uses 2 stop bits, 1 and 2 (even and odd) use 1 stop bit.

Not every code exists on every family: the manual's support columns could not be read reliably, so check the notes in each description. The manual marks M02 to M04, M08, M22, M28 to M30, M34, M66 and M67 as missing on three of the four families (they are left out here), and M07, M33 and M63 to M65 as missing on one.

alarm.8: Overvoltage at constant speed or stopping (0u3)
alarm.51: Data save error on insufficient voltage (erf)

comm_error.1: Run for the timer, then alarm stop
comm_error.2: Run for the timer, continue if communications recover, else alarm stop

link_mode.0: Frequency and operation per H30 and y98
link_mode.2: Frequency per H30 and y98, operation from communications
link_mode.3: Frequency from communications, operation per H30 and y98
